title: aaps-ci.yml does‘t allow line breaks in KEYSTORE_BASE64
body:
Please change the line

echo "KEYSTORE_BASE64=${{ secrets.KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV

to

echo "KEYSTORE_BASE64<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_ENV
echo "${{ secrets.KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_ENV

or something else, so that line breaks in the secret KEYSTORE_BASE64 created during base64 encoding of the keystore.jks witch certutil would work.

Thanks in advance.
Kind regards.

comments.body:
@Angus-repo 
>May I ask whether your BASE64 was generated using aaps-ci-preparation.html?

No, it was generated for my own AAPS workflow in 12/2024 on a Microsoft Windows maschine, using certutil in a cmd window, see https://github.com/winni67/AndroidAPS/blob/master/.github/workflows/Instruction-Build-version-to-Google-Drive.md
I believe the aaps-ci-preparation tools is an easier way, but I don‘t trust such tools, when they need passwords and secrets for my Google services. So, I decided to manually define these Github Secrets from existing ones and was astonished, that only one line and no multiple lines are allowed for these secrets.
Perhaps this small change can fix it for other people.
It‘s the same for GDRIVE_OAUTH2. Perhaps it would be easier, to split it into the both secrets GDRIVE_CLIENT_ID|GDRIVE_REFRESH_TOKEN, which are contained in this secret and store them in own secrets.
Thanks in advance.

Note 1: Google OAuth2 does not require the user's password. It only requires the user to consent to Google Drive write access. If a Google login screen appears, it means the default browser has never been logged into Google — you only need to log in once in your default browser.

Note 2: aaps-ci-preparation.html is an open-source tool, so its security is open to inspection and verification.
agree with @Angus-repo . We must support wiki methods. And the password is entered on Google's site, not localy
